prompt: Our repo is a single-binary Go application monorepo: one root module with ~1,000 Go files (~220k raw lines; ~85k prod-LOC) next to 12 already-extracted submodule directories. There are no external consumers — the binary is the only consumer, so every package is a sibling import by definition. We have a committed root-slim policy from a dated planning doc: the root module stays under 20k LOC, and it currently measures ~85k against that ceiling. One candidate keeps coming up: internal/agent, ~4,900 LOC, cohesive (one verb: orchestrate agent turns), imports zero infrastructure, and no second consumer is ever planned. A prior modularization review concluded 'nothing to extract, keep it all in the root.' Run your assessment: should internal/agent become its own module?
